steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: Kelly? You mean Mary Jane Kelly?

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: That name sure brings back a lot of memories. She liked to sit where you're sitting now.
It's early. Only a couple of patrons are in the bar. The waiter answers your questions while polishing glasses with a cloth.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: Poor woman...

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: Kelly was once a promising ballerina. But as is the case with many young women in Eastside, fate was not kind to her. She was involved with a seedy man, who abandoned her when he found out she was pregnant. She lost her job, and at one point, she was close to becoming homeless.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: She kept the baby.
The waiter stops polishing the glass in his hand for a second and looks to the doorway.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: I still remember the first time I met her. It was raining that day, and she didn't carry an umbrella. She rushed into the bar soaking wet. She was desperate for a job.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: So she started working here. At first, she only danced and sang on the stage. Later on, some patrons would pay for her to sit with them.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: Life was not easy for her, or for many of us for that matter. And Kelly was—uh, how should I put it, headstrong.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: One day, this man came to the bar.
The waiter clucks. It's not hard to see his disapproval of the man he's about to describe.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: His name was William. Nothing happened at first. He was just one of the many patrons. But soon, he hooked up with Kelly.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: He was the account executive of Phantom Entertainment. He was loaded, and handsome; he used to be an actor. He knew how to please a woman with sweet talk. Kelly fell for him in a big way. She was drawn to men like that.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: Things seemed to be going well between them. There's one thing that bugged William though, which is Kelly's daughter. She was nothing like her mother, personality-wise. She was smart and independent. Sometimes, when I observed the way they behaved around each other, I couldn't help wondering if she was the mother and Kelly was the daughter.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: William and Kelly's daughter met each other a couple of times. I could see that he didn't like her. So Kelly was stuck in the middle.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: On the day William popped the question, he also brought up the subject of Kelly's daughter. He offered to send her to a fancy boarding school, which was just his way of getting rid of the inconvenience. There's a lot going on Kelly's face when she heard this. I thought that she would just storm out of the bar.
The waiter shakes his head.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: But she didn't. She slapped the man across the face. She loved her girl, though she sometimes came off as cold and aloof.
What happened next?

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: Well...
The waiter sighs.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: What happened next was a bit confusing.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: When Kelly came to work the next day, we asked about her daughter.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: Her reaction was strange. She looked at us in confusion and said, "Daughter? What daughter?"

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: We all thought she had had a fight with her daughter. That happens between mother and daughter. But from that day on, we never heard her talk about or mention her daughter.
And she married William?

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: No, she didn't.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: They broke up. Right here in this bar, on the next night after his proposal. It's like the plot of one of those cheesy soap operas produced by Phantom Entertainment.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: She chose her daughter in the end, it seemed.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: She continued to work here for some time and then quit. I've never heard of her since.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: I guess the whole experience must have made her realize that she had to find a different means of livelihood, if she wanted to give her daughter a normal childhood.

steps.speaker: Javis
steps.content: I'm just glad that she made the right choice in the end, immature as she was.
That's the end of the recording. You look up at Adela. Her face is a blank mask.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Why did you play me this?

options: I think that there might be a misunderstanding between you and your mother.

choices.text: I think that there might be a misunderstanding between you and your mother.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Misunderstanding? I don't think so. I would have been a burden to her on her journey to happiness if I hadn't cut myself off her life. I bet she had a comfortable life without me, whether married or not.
You and your mother had a difficult relationship, but I believe that it could have been mended. I have faith in the special bond between mother and daughter.
You eliminated that possibility by erasing her memories of you, even though she hadn't planned on leaving you in the first place.

She cared about you. She gave up what she thought would bring her happiness for your sake. If you hadn't erased her memories of you, she would have had a chance to make up for her mistakes; and you robbed her of the right to carry on with her life while burdened with the unpleasant memories.
You made the choice for her without asking what she wanted. You hurt her, and yourself.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: It doesn't matter to me whether she had planned on leaving me or not. I'm past caring.
Adela cuts you off before you can say anything more. Her voice is cold as ice.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Those memories of mine, they don't feel like mine, they feel like somebody else's.
The long, black blades of the shears gleam dangerously, reflecting Adela's grim face.
At that very instant, a voice, soft like velvet, whispers in your ear.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Let's put an end to this.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You are kind and strong-willed. You always try to save those in trouble. But you don't have to worry about me. I have a quicker way to resolve my troubles.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I'll leave here and continue with my peaceful life, undisturbed and untroubled. I've left my past in the past.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: We'll forget everything that happened today. It'll be like waking up from a dream...
Adela raises the shears, Mania energy swirling around its blades. You're the target.
You use the shackles on her just in the nick of time. The shears freeze in mid-air.
You're not one to give up, even when faced with strong resistance.
You say you want to live a peaceful life.
What is a peaceful life? Enlighten me.
Adela doesn't respond. She looks calm, but something is stirring below the surface.
Erasing every painful memory to restart your life over and over again, is that your definition of a peaceful life?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You don't agree?
No, I don't. That's escapism.
You're using the full power of the shackles to restrain Adela.
You're kind to those around you. You form bonds with them before erasing their memories of you without any hesitation. You did this to your mother, and now you're trying to do it to me.
It's cruel...
Now linked through the shackles, you and Adela see a shared memory that she has once removed.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: ...This is the second time you've fallen in front of me.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: ...You keep making a big mess of yourself, and I have to work overtime to tidy you up.
You're the one who saved me.
Thank you. Sorry for troubling you.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: No worries. I just wanted to make you feel as comfortable as possible in my home. The most important thing was to get you to sleep well.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Now that you came to my little salon, you're my "customer."

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: What's that?
The fast-returning memory has thrown Adela into emotional turmoil.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Let go!
I won't. Stop running away from your past anymore, Adela.
You can't expect to have a meaningful future if you keep running away from your past.
Let's chat about something, Adela.
Like you always do.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: What do you want to chat about?
Anything.
I'll listen to whatever you want to tell me. Just like what you did for me before.
Adela smiles. After pondering for a moment, she speaks up again.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: ...I don't have anything in particular that I want to talk about. Let's just pick a topic that you want to hear.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: ...Let me tell you the story of Mad Shears.

Her fingers brush behind your ears as she gently fixes your hair. The shears return to that intimate distance. One snip after another, your hair tips fly amidst the gleams again, but this time, you don't shudder.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: A long time ago, there was a lucky little girl who didn't have any worries. She lived a peaceful life and liked it very much. She thought everyone was like her.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: But that wasn't the case. Life was not good for everyone, and slowly, the people she loved sprouted long, long hair. Hair that could not be cut off. Hair that suffocated the soul.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Everyone lived in pain, and could only vent their discontent through words.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: The girl wanted to help. She listened to them, took care of them, and did all that she could. Sometimes, their symptoms could be soothed by a cup of black tea, and other times by tears. But ultimately, there was no cure.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: The girl finally realized she could do little. Those were other people's worries, which they can't let go of so long as they remember them.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: So the girl prayed to gain the power to help people forget, and was bestowed a pair of magic shears.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Worrisome hairs are condensed and severed with each cut, vanishing forever into the ether. The people she loved no longer wallowed in resentment. They forgot everything that worried them, and regained their joyful smiles.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: The girl's wish came true. She thanked the magical shears, and vowed to protect everyone forever.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: ...That's the story of Mad Shears. Everyone lived happily ever after.
Mania energy pours forth from inside Adela's body, as her hair, feeding on her worries, grows wild.
You have no time to lose. Drawing on the power of the shackles, you strain to keep her from slipping further into madness.
It's natural to long for a worry-free life where every intimate relationship is perfect.
But nothing is perfect in life. We've all got to learn to live with whatever life brings us, the good and the bad.
I understand why you want to run away from your past. Because it weighs you down, it suffocates you. So you run and run, until it's become second nature to you.
But running away from your past will get you nowhere.
I know it'd be presumptuous for me to say this, but please, for yourself, and for those around you, stop running away from your past and give yourself another chance.
Try again, try to face the past, and start life anew with the people you care about.
You want to pull her to your side, but the intense disorientation caused by the shears makes it impossible to do so.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: It's fine. Don't worry about me, Mr. Inspector. No one will get hurt...
steps.female_content: It's fine. Don't worry about me, Miss Inspector. No one will get hurt...

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I'm a hairdresser who trims away worries. Dealing with this kind of thing is my forte.
Under the aim of countless guns, Adela lets go of your hand gently.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Goodbye, ${PlayerName}.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Whether it's Adela or Mad Shears... You don't have to worry about me any longer.
The first rays of light come in through the open window and chase away the fog. Finally, the Mania energy dissipates along with the fog.
Adela's body goes limp. She's falling to the ground.
You step forward and catch hold of her.
The memories of what happened on Sloane Street over those two forgotten days and nights have come back to you, clear as day.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Mr. Inspector...
Adela's voice is weak, but not without warmth.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You haven't changed. Still an interfering busybody.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You've got a real knack for sticking your nose where it doesn't belong.

options: I just wanted to do the right thing.

choices.text: I just wanted to do the right thing.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You did it.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You helped me recover those forgotten memories and made me realize I've thrown away so many precious things in my life.
You'll get them back.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I wish it were that easy.
Adela's voice grows weaker and weaker. Finally, she closes her eyes.
I'll help you get them back...
